title: Why Bother Me Again? Benchmarking Personal Agent Memory for Interaction Preferences
abstract: arXiv:2610.30485v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Personal intelligence systems are taking on increasingly complex everyday tasks, yet repeated questions, unnecessary confirmations, and unwanted outreach can turn capable assistance into interaction burden. Reducing this burden requires agents to remember how users want to be assisted. However, existing memory benchmarks focus on factual recall and personalized answers and rarely test how agents learn and act on interaction preferences. We introduce MemPABench, an interactive environment for on-policy evaluation of memory in personal agents. MemPABench poses long-horizon tasks requiring agents to decide when to clarify, confirm, or act autonomously. Four grounded simulated users hold 14 preferences across work and personal contexts. Their feedback spans 99 sessions over four months, with five event-driven changes per user testing memory updates. We evaluate preference selection, delivered behavior, and sensitivity to context and prefer

translated_title: 为什么要再次打扰我？面向交互偏好的个人智能体记忆基准测试
translated_abstract: 个人智能系统正在承担日益复杂的日常任务，然而重复的提问、不必要的确认和不想要的主动打扰，会把强大的辅助能力变成交互负担。要减少这种负担，需要智能体记住用户希望被协助的方式。然而，现有的记忆基准主要关注事实回忆和个性化回答，很少测试智能体如何学习并落实交互偏好。我们提出了MemPABench，一个用于个人智能体记忆在线评估的交互式环境。MemPABench设置了需要智能体决定何时澄清、何时确认、何时自主行动的长期任务。四个基于真实场景的模拟用户在工作和个人场景中持有14项偏好。他们的反馈横跨四个月内的99个会话，且每个用户有五个由事件驱动的偏好变化，用于测试记忆的更新能力。我们评估了偏好选择、实际执行行为，以及对上下文和偏好的敏感度。
tldr: 提出了MemPABench——一个评估个人智能体记忆与落实用户交互偏好能力的在线交互式基准，通过四个月的模拟用户会话和动态偏好变化，测试智能体何时澄清、确认或自主行动。
en_tdlr: Introduces MemPABench, an interactive on-policy benchmark that evaluates how personal agents memorize and act on users' interaction preferences across long-horizon tasks, simulated users, and evolving preferences over four months.
